prerequisites: §24 of the Study and Examination Regulations (Part A)

learning_outcomes.text: Students demonstrate in their Bachelor's theses that they are able to independently process a problem scientifically and methodically within a given period.
Students acquire the ability to present and analyze the state of the art.
Students acquire the ability to apply methods learned during their studies for processing a scientific question.

syllabus_topics: Detailed literature review: In-depth analysis and critical examination of existing specialist literature.
Methodological implementation: Application of chosen research methods to answer the research question.
Data acquisition and evaluation: Systematic collection, documentation, and evaluation of data (depending on the type of work).
Structuring the work: Development of a clear outline (e.g., introduction, theory, methodology, results, discussion, conclusion).
Writing the work: Precise and comprehensible presentation of results and argumentation according to scientific standards.
Reflecting on intermediate results: Regular review and, if necessary, adjustment of the approach based on new findings.
Utilizing supervision: Active communication with the supervisor for uncertainties or interim coordination.
Observing formalities: Consistent adherence to citation rules, creation of correct figures, tables, directories, and appendices.
Time management: Continuous monitoring of the schedule and timely planning for corrections and formatting.
Preparation for submission: Final check of the work for completeness, linguistic quality, and formal correctness.
